title: Temple of Bel
visualBrief: Surviving Temple of Bel ruin at Palmyra: approximately200m enclosed temenos with fortified west gate, selected perimeter columns/stumps, exposed central cella podium, standing monumental cella doorway and a field of fallen blocks/drums. The cella roof, walls and complete surrounding temple colonnade destroyed in2015 remain absent. Independent Palmyra monuments and modern visitor buildings remain native.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Q797481/way226891786 identifies the complete temenos boundary. Its original16 vertices are retained at the mapped anchor, with a4.589-degree internal rotation and west gate on the western boundary. PMTiles building35184675160368 supplies four original central cella/podium corners. That coarse generic building record is replaced by the surviving ruin, not extruded into the lost temple. Standing cella doorway position follows the west long side; exact doorway offset and surviving perimeter column positions are picture-guided estimates.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: The ordinary article gives15m for the original temple and describes the cella destruction with surviving doorway, fortified gate and outer walls.2016/2018 pictures show the isolated rectangular doorway above rubble. The modeled doorway cornice rises11.15m above the conservative podium datum, horns12.1m. The west gate is approximately12.2m above adjacent coarse grade, most outer walls5.7m and west walls7.3–10m. Perimeter standing columns7.6m and stumps1.2–3.15m are schematic. Exact damage, block positions, temple heights and column survival were not surveyed.

nativeTerrainClearance.basis: Every vertex of every original rendered6m grid cell intersecting each occupied floor bounding rectangle is included. Triangle interpolation stays below each opaque floor, so original terrain can remain intact under and around the model.

Only the small mapped central cella footprint has an opaque podium floor; its top clears every original rendered grid-cell vertex in its bounds by0.2m. Outer walls, gate, perimeter stumps and scattered rubble use local standard DEM grade and extend slightly below it. No ground or water cutout is needed; the open court keeps its original terrain. Gate threshold and individual stones remain approximate.
